title: Geometric representation of finite constant ring towers
statement: For any scheme morphism f:X→Y and a natural-number opposite diagram Q of finite commutative rings in the sheaf-value universe, there exist a diagram D of objects of the small pro-etale site of Y and a cone c on D such that c is limiting, its image under site base change along f is limiting, and the diagram of lifted Yoneda sheaves of D is naturally isomorphic to the underlying set sheaves of Q followed by the constant ring-sheaf functor. No surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 097D, lemma-construct-profinite; Tag 098T, lemma-morphism-big-small (2); profinite test objects of RefactorInstruction.tex Section 4, Lemma lem:XS.

proof.text: Shrink the finite carriers to the scheme universe, transporting every transition by equivShrink. The lifted finite-carrier diagram is naturally isomorphic to the original carrier diagram.

Take its limit as a diagram of finite discrete profinite spaces. The opposite locally constant integer ring functor is a right adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-locally-constant-right-adjoint]; Spec also preserves limits. Pass to schemes over Spec Z, then base change to Y. The resulting cone is a limit in Over Y and hence in its full pro-etale subcategory. Base change again along f preserves the same cone in Over X, and fullness reflects the limit.

Use the natural finite-test-object comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor], and explicitly compare chosen slice coproducts with scheme coproducts. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-constant-representable] naturally to the resulting finite-copy diagram. Compose with the carrier shrink isomorphism and Mathlib constantCommuteCompose to identify the underlying ring sheaves.
